課程綱要.課程目標: The primary objective of this course is to provide a rigorous and comprehensive understanding of simulation and Monte Carlo methods for statistical computing and modern data analysis. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical implementation. By the end of the course, students will be able to: (1) Understand the theoretical principles underlying random number generation and simulation techniques, including pseudo-random number generators and methods for generating non-uniform distributions. (2) Implement classical Monte Carlo methods such as inverse transform sampling, rejection sampling, importance sampling, and bootstrap procedures. (3) Analyze Monte Carlo estimators in terms of bias, variance, consistency, and convergence properties, including the Law of Large Numbers and the Central Limit Theorem. (4) Apply variance reduction techniques, such as antithetic variables, control variates, and stratified sampling, to improve simulation efficiency. (5) Understand the theory and practice of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, including the Metropolis–Hastings algorithm and Gibbs sampling. (6) Evaluate convergence diagnostics and mixing behavior of Markov chains in practical statistical applications. (7) Use simulation-based approaches for statistical inference, including Bayesian computation and complex likelihood-based problems. (8) Develop efficient and reproducible simulation algorithms using R, and assess computational accuracy, stability, and performance. (9) Critically assess the strengths and limitations of simulation-based methods in modern statistical research.
課程綱要.授課內容:
Random Numbers (Chapter 3).
Pseudo-Random Number Generations (Chapters 4–6).
Statistical Analysis of Simulated Data (Chapter 8).
Variance Reduction Techniques (Chapters 9).
Statistical Validation Techniques (Chapter 11).
Markov Chain Monte Carlo Methods (Chapter 12)
Variance Inference (VI)
課程綱要.教科書/參考書: 1. Ross, S. M. (2013), Simulation (5th Edition) (Wiley). References: 2. Rizzo, M. (2019), Statistical Computing with R (2nd Ed.) (Chapman & Hall). 3. Robert, C. and Casella, G. (2004), Monte Carlo Statistical Methods (Springer).

9 Midterm Exam
10 Model Assessment and Selection

13 Multidimensional Scaling
14 Principal Components: Curves and Surfaces
15 Cluster Analysis
16 Visualization
17 Partial least Sqaure and SEM analysis
